01.text: Provable, not visible. This is how the attested market is built.

02.text: It starts with one decision. The chain is a notary and a settlement rail, not a database.

03.text: On chain goes only what must be verified later, without trusting us: commitments, identities, grants, signatures, settlement state, and the audit log root.

04.text: Anything someone needs to read stays off chain: records, mandates, the matching engine, models, documents. And keys never leave a hardware security module.

06.text: Around that ledger sit eight services. Identity, ingestion, the record store, attestation. Matching, settlement, the agent runtime, and integration.

07.text: Every service writes commitments to the ledger, and reads grants from it. None of them stores state there.

09.text: Now, follow one record. A rent roll leaves the owner's property system through an adapter. Ingestion extracts its fields, with lineage back to the source.

10.text: The record store encrypts each field under its own key, in the owner's vault.

11.text: Each field is hashed with a random salt, because N-O-I equals eight hundred thousand is guessable. An unsalted hash is a leak.

12.text: The hashes roll up into a single Merkle root, per asset, per period.

13.text: Attestation collects signatures from independent sources of the fact, computes the quorum and a level, and commits.

14.text: What reaches the chain is the root, the signatures and the level. The rent roll itself never does.

15.text: Two quorums, kept apart. Consensus orders: validators agree what happened, and when. Attestation verifies: independent sources sign that a fact is true enough to act on.

16.text: The validators are named parties, like notaries, auditors and banks, anchored to a public chain that no consortium member controls.

17.text: A buyer's agent gets a grant: the value and salt for named fields only. It checks them against the root on chain, and the grant itself is logged.

18.text: Where the double-blind market needs it, a range proof answers: is N-O-I at least X? Without revealing it.

19.text: Every action traces to a person: institution, principal, agent credential, action. Agents prepare. Anything that binds also carries a principal's signature.

20.text: Matching runs deterministically in an attested enclave, with roots in and a root out. Neutrality becomes verifiable.

21.text: List, diligence, match, finance, settle. Each step leaves a mark on chain a regulator can verify, without seeing a rent, a mandate or a price. And operate repeats it, monthly.

22.text: None of this asks an intermediary to change their systems. First, shadow: adapters read what exists. Then, write back, in their own format. Then, they work on the platform, because it's faster.

23.text: Every adapter is one untrusted source. A compromised adapter can lie. It cannot reach a quorum alone.

24.text: A bank gets three connectors: its financing pack in, its credit policy out, and a servicing feed. Neither bank system is replaced.

25.text: Safety starts with a split. A data breach costs confidentiality; a key compromise is money gone. So data and value sit on different keys, networks and teams.

26.text: And assume a key will be compromised. Alone, it can do nothing. With a second, only a little. And with a third, it can be reversed.

27.text: Commit first. Connect second. Match third. Settle last.
